<!-- pr-reviewer: c93678aa038656a782274da34b06f22a5638a633 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (stacked on #1136 -> #1131 -> #560 -> #551; those merge first, parent-first, retargeting this one to main before its parent merges).

Reviewed only the PR's own change (`pr-1136...pr-1156`, 16 files, all additions, no existing line removed). It touches no build.rs, `.github`, scripts, Cargo.toml, process files, CHANGELOG or snapshot PNGs.

**What looks good**
- `sinker_cavity::cavity_of`: every face is checked alone (finite, range, planar, area, closed loop), then classed by normal. Walls are matched to the floor ring edge by edge with an interval cover, so a wall that stops short, faces away, reaches below the floor or stands on another cavity is each refused by name. Leaning is refused past 1e-6, and a floor that is not level is refused.
- `sinker_electrode::derive`: the rectangle is read off the picked ring's own corners (so a rounded corner under the inset cannot pass), then the Clipper2 offset must agree with `cavity - 2*(undersize+orbit)` within 1e-5. I found no accepted-but-wrong cavity. The inset check, the 1 um minimum side and stub, `length > depth` and the 500 mm bound are all in order. `standing_in` clips the facets against the full column above the floor, so a boss, rib or overhang refuses with the spot.
- Fuzz (`sinker_electrode_fuzz.rs`): fixed xorshift seeds, 6000 sound cavities each damaged 1 of 20 named ways, and every one must refuse with its own named text (not just "no panic"). The sound cavity is checked first, so the damage is what flips it. 20000 garbage sets are checked for finite, sane output, and the test also bounds how many answer at all. Runs in 0.06 s for all 7 motion tests.
- Command and MCP: `ElectrodeFromFaces` validates at construction and delegates apply/invert to `AddTool`, so one undo removes the tool. `undersize` xor `condition` is enforced (both and neither each refused by name, tested). The `burn` reply goes into `add_operation` as is, and the MCP test does exactly that.
- Done-means sim test goes through `simulate_document`, and the off-centre contrast (+1 mm) is convicted with max gouge > 0.5 mm.
- Laws: provenance on every module, decision file present, no unwrap/expect/panic in the new non-test code, all files under 400 lines, `Changelog:` and `Fixes #547` in the body. The change is append-only (module registrations and the MCP table).

**Local results** (trial merge with current upstream/main was clean; debug, own target, sccache)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| app `sinker_electrode` | 8 passed |
| app `sinker_electrode_mcp` | 1 passed |
| app `sinker_burn` / `sinker_undersize` | 7 / 5 passed |
| app `mcp` / `mcp_pick` / `mcp_pockets` | 18 / 6 / 3 passed |
| app `commands_undo` / `tool_law` / `pocket_recognition` | 30 / 4 / 11 passed |
| app `edm_conditions` / `edm_machine` | 6 / 7 passed |
| motion `--lib` | 205 passed, 1 ignored (7 sinker_electrode incl. both fuzz tests) |
| app `--lib` | 138 passed |
| clippy motion + app `--all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. A floor face with an inner ring is accepted (the decision file says a hole is harmless and the column test tells it from a boss). Fine for the box electrode; #1152 should revisit it when the body electrode lands.
2. The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is a process file and is left to a later process PR, as the decision file says.
3. Orbit is a documented hook only until #544; the tool reply says so.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: dcaa3a36ed40faaf42df47c0a5909234f6b343dd -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge - but only the ones it inherits from its stack.** This PR's own change (`c93678aa`, the diff over #1136's head `b93e8fbe`: 16 files, +1904) has no blocking findings. It targets `main` and its diff includes #560 -> #1131 -> #1136, so merging it today would also land those PRs' open blockers. Once they are fixed and merged, this needs only a short re-check of the delta.

This is the first independent review of this PR. The earlier `pr-reviewer:` comments came from the author's account, so I read them as the author's claims and checked everything against the code.

### What looks good
- **The cavity read is strict, with no guessing** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_cavity.rs`). Each face is checked on its own: finite, in range, planar, non-zero area by Newell's vector area, closed. Faces are then sorted into floor and walls by their outward normal. Each wall has to stand on a floor edge at floor height, rise above the floor and face into it, and together the walls must cover every floor edge end to end (interval cover, `:282-306`). A boss's outside walls, a second floor, a wall from another cavity, a shelf's open edge and a drafted or curved wall are all refused, each with a message naming it.
- **Size and sign are right.** The undersize is per side: `face = cavity - 2 x (undersize + orbit)` (`sinker_electrode.rs:195-196`). The Clipper2 offset is only used to cross-check that arithmetic (within 10 nm), not as a second source of the size. A finish electrode made from F1's 0.02 passes #543's size law, and the program verdict comes out clean.
- **Rectangles only, refused by name otherwise.** Only an axis-aligned rectangle is accepted. The rectangle test runs on the picked outline itself, not on the offset, so a rounded pocket whose corner radius is smaller than the inset still gets refused. That is the right call: a box atom with sharp corners in a filleted pocket would cut into the fillets.
- **Obstructions in the cavity's column are caught.** `standing_in` clips every part facet against the cavity's column above the floor (Sutherland-Hodgman). The column is open upward, so a boss, a rib or an overhang across the mouth (an undercut) refuses the electrode and the message gives the spot. The cavity's own walls and floor are kept out by the 0.1 um clearance.
- **Placement.** Picks go through `pick::check_pickable` (#692). A welded patch counts as a curved wall, and a chain or vertex is refused. Vertices and normals are brought into world space with the model's `Location`, and the reply says `"frame": "world"`, the same as `list_features` and `find_pockets`.
- **Command and MCP.** `ElectrodeFromFaces` validates everything when it is created; its `apply`/`invert` are `AddTool`'s, so one undo removes the tool. MCP `electrode_from_faces` ships with it. It takes `undersize` or `condition`, never both and never neither. Its `burn` object is accepted as-is by `add_operation`, and the MCP test pins that.
- **Prime Directive.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Indexing goes through `get`, and the spec numbers are checked (negative, NaN and infinite values are refused, and so is an inset that consumes the cavity). The seeded fuzz runs 6000 named damage cases and 20000 garbage face sets.
- **Rules and housekeeping.** Every new module has a provenance line naming public sources (Joshi & Chang, Newell/Sutherland, Sutherland-Hodgman, Clipper2), with no vendor material. All files are under 400 lines. Layering is kept: pure geometry in `motion`, glue in `app`, no new components, no UI touched. No snapshot PNGs, `CHANGELOG.md`, process files, `build.rs` or dependencies are changed. The decisions file is `docs/decisions/547-electrode-from-faces.md`. Commits use conventional subjects, and the body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #547`.

### Local results (head `dcaa3a36`, which already contains current `origin/main` `62a2c93a`, so the trial merge was "already up to date"; debug, Windows)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` | 207 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored |
| `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode` | 8 passed |
| `--test sinker_electrode_mcp` | 1 passed |
| `--test sinker_burn` / `sinker_undersize` | 7 / 5 passed |
| `--test mcp` / `mcp_pick` / `mcp_pockets` | 18 / 6 / 3 passed |
| `--test commands_undo` / `tool_law` / `pocket_recognition` | 30 / 4 / 11 passed |
| `--test stock_sim_document` / `edm_conditions` / `edm_machine` | 9 / 1 / 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --lib` | fails: inherited from #1131, see below (this PR touches no UI) |

I also ran throwaway probes locally; they were not pushed.
- **Part rotated 90 deg about Z and moved (100, 50, 3):** the electrode came out 11.96 x 19.96 (X and Y swapped as expected), centred at (104, 56), floor 17, top 23. The finish burn left the program verdict clean, with 0 gouge and 0 rest.
- **Part rotated 15 deg:** refused as non-rectangular, and the message names #1152.
- **Undersize 0 with a single burn:** the 0.5 mm spark gap was convicted by the verdict (60 gouge cells); a 0.02 gap was under the sim's resolution.
- **Bad spec numbers:** a negative undersize, an infinite orbit and an undersize of 1e300 were each refused by name.

I did not run the full quick-gate plan (about 190 app suites and 7 UI suites, chosen because `commands/mod.rs`, `operation/mod.rs` and `mcp/mod.rs` each gained one line). The change only adds code, and I ran the suites covering what it touches.

### Requested before merge
This PR's own changes need nothing. Its inherited blockers, already raised on its parents and not repeated here: (a) the UI crate does not compile (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_icons.rs:17`, `ToolKind::Electrode` is missing from the match; I reproduced this at this head); (b) a Sinker Burn posts milling G-code through the default Fanuc post (#1131); (c) #1131's plunge can feed upward when the gap is large. When those are fixed on #1131/#1136 and the stack merges in order, this PR can merge right after #1136.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `crates/app/src/operation/sinker_faces.rs:123-127`: if `model::world_facets` returns `None`, the obstruction check falls back to an empty facet list and passes without a word. That cannot happen in practice, because the faces were just resolved from the same model. Still, refusing ("the part's facets could not be read") would match the Prime Directive's rule to never silence.
2. `standing_in` checks only the picked part. A clamp or fixture over the cavity is left to the stock sim and the fixture checks. That is fine, and could be one line in the decisions file.
3. An undersize of 0 is accepted. That is legitimate input, and the verdict convicts a full-size electrode once the gap is large enough to resolve. A by-name warning for `undersize == 0` on a condition with a non-zero gap could be a P7 follow-up.
4. The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table still has no `electrode_from_faces` row. Leaving process files out of a feature PR is right, but the owed row should be a `P5` `area:mcp` follow-up issue (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool") so it doesn't get lost. Could you file it, or should the maintainer?
5. Orbit is taken off the electrode but not yet accounted for in #543's size law. The reply says so, and that errs on the safe side (an under-size finish gets refused). #544 owns the fix.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
